# Region Nordjylland — Nordjylland

Region Nordjylland and Nordjylland represent the organizational and geographic dimensions, respectively, of the northernmost administrative area in [[danmark|Danmark]]. As a location, Nordjylland is one of the five Danish regions, encompassing major healthcare facilities such as [[aalborg-universitetshospital|Aalborg Universitetshospital]] and [[regionshospital-nordjylland|Regionshospital Nordjylland]] [^src13]. As an organization, Region Nordjylland is the administrative body responsible for healthcare delivery and data reporting to the [[akut-kirurgi-databasen|Akut Kirurgi Databasen]], which is published by the [[regionerne-kliniske-kvalitetsudviklingsprogram]] [^src1].

The connection between the geographic area and its governing organization is critical for understanding regional healthcare performance in acute surgery. Data from the Akut Kirurgi Databasen tracks various quality indicators across the country, allowing for direct comparisons between Nordjylland and other regions like [[region-hovedstaden|Region Hovedstaden]], [[region-midtjylland|Region Midtjylland]], [[region-sjaelland|Region Sjælland]], and [[region-syddanmark|Region Syddanmark]].

For [[indikator-1|Indikator 1]], which measures specific acute surgery performance metrics, the geographic area of Nordjylland showed a fulfillment rate of 29.3% (95% CI: 23.7–35.5) for the period of September 1, 2022, to August 31, 2023 [^src10]. In the subsequent period from September 1, 2023, to August 31, 2024, the fulfillment rate for Indikator 1 in Region Nordjylland improved to 36.7% (95% CI: 30.4–43.4) [^src15]. 

Regional variations are evident across multiple indicators. For [[indikator-5y|Indikator 5y]], the proportion varied regionally from 9.0% in Region Nordjylland to 19.9% in Region Hovedstaden [^src1]. For [[indikator-5|Indikator 5]], which tracks intermediate admissions, the share ranged from 17.2% in Region Nordjylland to 27.0% in Region Syddanmark [^src5]. The region also recorded the highest 30-day mortality for [[indikator-10|Indikator 10]] in the 2023 report, with the proportion varying from 9.9% in Region Midtjylland to 14.1% in Region Nordjylland [^src2]. In the 2024 report, the share for Indikator 10 varied from 15.7% in Region Sjælland to 19.6% in Region Nordjylland [^src18]. 

Other indicators highlight further regional disparities. The proportion for [[indikator-6|Indikator 6]] varied from 20.3% in Region Nordjylland to 46.4% in Region Midtjylland [^src6]. For [[indikator-7|Indikator 7]], it ranged from 6.8% in Region Nordjylland to 33.1% in Region Hovedstaden [^src16]. For [[indikator-8|Indikator 8]], the share varied from 41.9% in Region Nordjylland to 56.8% in Region Syddanmark [^src17]. Additionally, a supplementary indicator showed that 21 out of 93 patients in Nordjylland were operated on within 6 hours for perforation, ischemia, or bleeding, corresponding to a proportion of 22.6% (95% CI: 14.6–32.4) for [[indikator-5x]] [^src11].

Mortality and patient demographics provide further context. In Nordjylland, 13 out of 76 patients died within 30 days after acute surgery with a [[charlson-score-1-2|Charlson Score = 1 eller 2]], representing 17.1% (95% CI: 9.4-27.5) [^src13]. Despite these variations in outcomes and processes, supplementary analyses show that the [[asa-score|ASA]] score for operated patients is not significantly different across the regions [^src8], and there is no significant difference in patient [[alder]] (age) among the regions [^src14]. 

Region Nordjylland actively participates in the national quality assurance process, having reported back that it had no comments on the annual report for the Akut Kirurgi Databasen [^src3]. In the 2024 report, further breakdowns showed that Region Nordjylland mobilized only 20.3% within 24 hours [^src9], with other specific metrics reaching 6.8% [^src9], 41.9% [^src9], and 14.0% [^src9].
